### Season outlook as written in the guide (p. 310)

The hope for Texas this season is that Steve Sarkisian does not have to embark on another campaign in hopes of getting his team into the College Football Playoff. Instead, the Longhorns are hoping to earn a seat at the table the old- fashioned way: by winning football games. Texas brings back one of the most experienced rosters in the country. Sixteen starters are back from last season, including quarterback Arch Manning. The team’s biggest weakness — offensive line — has been addressed. Two seasons ago, Sarkisian took Quinn Ewers to the CFP and won two games. It would be shocking if he cannot get this Texas team to the dance in 2026. Over 9.5 Phil Steele ranks Texas’ schedule as the hardest in the country, and there is obviously some truth to that. The Longhorns must face Ohio State in Week 2, Oklahoma on a neutral site and it must go to both LSU and Texas A&M. However, the devil is in the details for the Longhorns. Texas leaves the state just once from the beginning of the season until November, when it goes to face Tennessee. The meeting with the Buckeyes is a revenge spot in Austin. The yearly meeting with Oklahoma is in Dallas. Sure, the three- week stretch of Oklahoma, Florida and Ole Miss is difficult, but the Longhorns have a bye prior to the Red River Shootout, and the other two will be at home. If this is a true national title contender, 10 wins should be an attainable goal. So too should a national championship.

## 26. Open Questions / Risks

The guide's *Three Burning Questions for the 2026 Season* *(p. 311)*, with the answers as written:

### Does Arch Manning pick up where he left off?

There were many who were disappointed by the season Manning put together, but over the last six games he looked every bit of the blue-chip prospect he was lauded to be. In those contests, Manning threw 14 touchdowns with a turnover-worthy play rate of just 1.2%. He averaged 7.8 yards per attempt and added another five touchdowns on the ground. Texas went 5-1 SU/3-2-1 ATS in those games. For the season, Manning was the eighth-best passer in the conference by PFF standards and barely completed 60% of his passes. But if he can pick up on the form he had by season’s end, this offense could be more explosive.

### Will the offensive line improve in both facets?

In part, Manning struggled due to the pressure he faced. Manning was pressured on 35.6% of his dropbacks last season. His 165 dropbacks under pressure were the most in the SEC. In the running game, the issues were clear. Texas averaged 4.2 yards per carry and 138 yards per game in 2025. In order to fix the issues, Sarkisian helped his group by hitting the portal, bringing in a few bodies, but right tackle Melvin Siani from Wake Forest was the crown jewel. Couple that with the return of left tackle Trevor Goosby and center Connor Robertson, and this unit should be able to provide better protection for Manning while also giving more push in the run game.

### Can the secondary be a bigger strength?

During SEC media days, the Longhorns got a big win when five-star cornerback — and ESPN’s top-ranked 2027 corner — John Meredith III reclassified into the 2026 cycle in order to enroll for the fall. It’s unknown what role he will play, but a talent like that is never a negative, especially for a unit looking for more. Texas was 66th in defensive success rate against the pass last season and 33rd in opponent EPA per play through the air. Jelani McDonald (80 tackles, 3 pass breakups, 3 interceptions) is back at safety, but the defensive backfield lost three starters. Will Muschamp was also hired to run this defense in the offseason. There should be some improvement with this group overall.
